{
  "subtype": "faceted_decomposition",
  "concept": "airline_competitive_advantage",
  "per_column": [
    {"name": "crew_service_quality", "is_constitutive_facet": true, "role": "facet", "rationale": "Service quality is a genuine constitutive aspect of an airline's competitive advantage."},
    {"name": "crew_proactive_care", "is_constitutive_facet": true, "role": "facet", "rationale": "A dimension of the service experience; a real aspect of the advantage, though it overlaps heavily with crew_service_quality (both capture crew service excellence)."},
    {"name": "cultural_service_ethos", "is_constitutive_facet": true, "role": "facet", "rationale": "The style/character of service is an aspect of the service offering, hence part of competitive advantage, but again overlaps the service cluster."},
    {"name": "food_beverage_quality", "is_constitutive_facet": true, "role": "facet", "rationale": "Catering quality is a constitutive part of the product offering that drives advantage."},
    {"name": "meal_variety", "is_constitutive_facet": true, "role": "facet", "rationale": "A sub-aspect of the catering offering; a real part but overlaps with food_beverage_quality."},
    {"name": "seat_comfort_assessment", "is_constitutive_facet": true, "role": "facet", "rationale": "Seat comfort is a constitutive aspect of the physical product/hard-product advantage."},
    {"name": "seat_product_type", "is_constitutive_facet": true, "role": "facet", "rationale": "The hard-product type is an aspect of the seating offering; overlaps with seat_comfort_assessment as a seating cluster."},
    {"name": "special_service_recovery", "is_constitutive_facet": true, "role": "facet", "rationale": "Service recovery is a legitimate aspect of the service experience, part of the advantage; overlaps the service cluster."},
    {"name": "value_for_money_perception", "is_constitutive_facet": true, "role": "facet", "rationale": "Value-for-money is a constitutive commercial facet of competitive advantage, distinct from product/service quality."}
  ],
  "facet_columns": ["crew_service_quality", "crew_proactive_care", "cultural_service_ethos", "food_beverage_quality", "meal_variety", "seat_comfort_assessment", "seat_product_type", "special_service_recovery", "value_for_money_perception"],
  "non_facet_columns": [],
  "mutual_exclusivity": 0.5,
  "exhaustiveness": 0.6,
  "rationale": "All nine columns are genuine constitutive facets (part-of aspects) of airline competitive advantage rather than external predictors or causes, so the meronymy requirement is met. However mutual exclusivity is weak: the set clusters into three heavily overlapping groups -- service (crew_service_quality, crew_proactive_care, cultural_service_ethos, special_service_recovery), catering (food_beverage_quality, meal_variety), and seating (seat_comfort_assessment, seat_product_type) -- with several columns capturing the same underlying aspect under different names. Exhaustiveness is moderate: soft product (service, food, seat) and value are well covered, but key advantage aspects such as network/route connectivity, schedule/punctuality/reliability, inflight entertainment/connectivity, baggage/loyalty program, and price competitiveness are absent, leaving the concept only partially decomposed."
}
